task_origin_contract.rule: A free-discovery output cannot lose its candidate lifecycle by being repackaged as an ordinary taskbook. If the task exists because of a free candidate, its audited candidate provenance is mandatory.

obvious_stage_continuation_rule.pattern: STAGE integer >= 2 in task_id or title
obvious_stage_continuation_rule.reason: Stage numbering is explicit continuation semantics and may not be relabeled NEW_DIRECTION to bypass the successor gate.

task_lineage_contract.semantic_anti_evasion_rule: Even without Stage naming, if the parent result is a necessary research premise/motivation and the new task is the next unresolved layer of the same mother route, classify it CONTINUATION. Renaming does not reset lineage.
task_lineage_contract.rule: PASS or DONE on a parent task is not itself evidence for a successor. A CONTINUATION taskbook is publishable only when its successor gate names a genuine new information gap, falsifiable outcomes, a stop rule, and whether an independent/alternative exploration path was considered.

rules: TASKBOOK_POLICY_REVIEW_PASS != SCHEDULER_READY
A policy-approved taskbook remains base_state=DRAFT; only Scheduler V2 APPROVE creates runtime READY.
A Driver-approved taskbook must be PUBLISHed to Scheduler V2 before it can enter the live queue.
The publisher cannot APPROVE the same publication; cross-Driver review is mandatory.
Research completion uses SUBMIT followed by a cross-Driver REVIEW; the executor cannot close their own return.
A FREE researcher may PUBLISH a non-dispatchable task proposal directly into REVIEW_PENDING, but cannot create READY authority or self-approve it.
A task artifact found outside the live registry is an ORPHANED registry item until an explicit V2 event reconciles it.

optional_metadata.identity_lane: compact human-readable lane such as R012, R005C, P017
optional_metadata.parent_task_id: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null
optional_metadata.successor_gate: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null

manual_dispatch_identity_gate: Manual relay is only a transport fallback. It must still create the corresponding Scheduler V2 publication/approval/claim events; chat handoff alone cannot create runtime READY authority.
rules: A taskbook defines task-specific work, not a particular conversation instance and not a copy of repository operating policy.
Every newly authored or re-reviewed taskbook carries final_response_identity_policy=INHERIT_GLOBAL.
Every newly authored or re-reviewed taskbook carries scheduler_registration=ENTERPRISE_MATH_SCHEDULER_TASK_REGISTRATION_V2 and remains base_state=DRAFT before publication.
Every newly authored taskbook declares task origin and task lineage. A free-candidate origin preserves audited candidate provenance; a continuation preserves parent/successor provenance.
CONTINUATION requires parent_task_id and a complete successor_gate; stage numbering or parent PASS is never a substitute for the gate.
An obvious Stage 2+ task is CONTINUATION by construction and cannot be labeled NEW_DIRECTION merely to bypass the gate.
The taskbook body inherits current repository policy through research_taskbook_policy.json; generic rules already visible to the executing researcher must not be restated in the body.
Taskbook authoring uses tools/research_taskbook.py new, followed by task-local editing, machine audit, Driver policy review, and an approved policy_review stamp before Scheduler V2 publication.

The policy_review digest is derived from the current policy set. If any policy input changes, a previously stamped taskbook becomes stale and must be re-reviewed before another publication or redispatch.
Scheduler V2 is a policy input. A scheduler semantic change therefore invalidates old dispatch stamps rather than silently changing task execution semantics.
Task-specific instructions that conflict with inherited policy are forbidden unless recorded as a narrow temporary_overrides entry.
Legacy taskbooks remain historical artifacts, but V2 discovers task-like artifacts outside the live registry as ORPHANED instead of silently making them READY.
Taskbooks never bind a fixed runtime Researcher-ID. Runtime identity belongs to Scheduler V2 CLAIM/ADOPT or a separately registered direct/manual transport envelope.
A continuation in the same researcher conversation preserves its existing Researcher-ID; a genuinely new dispatch receives a new identity unless explicitly routed to the same conversation.
Researcher identity never grants Driver authority or theorem ownership. Driver conversations use Driver-ID.

A free-research axiom candidate enters Driver-approved taskbook authoring only after Phase-B audit and Driver intake, but a FREE researcher may publish a non-dispatchable REVIEW_PENDING task proposal without pretending it is already Driver-approved.
recommended_flow: write only task-local mathematical/research content and complete origin/lineage metadata
verify the taskbook still has base_state=DRAFT and a V2 scheduler_registration marker
publisher emits Scheduler V2 PUBLISH with immutable taskbook ref
a different Driver emits REVIEW_CLAIM then APPROVE
only after Scheduler runtime state READY may an executor CLAIM
executor finishes with SUBMIT, not DONE
a different Driver claims RETURN_REVIEW and emits REVIEW verdict
lease-expired or externally discovered tasks are recovered through ORPHAN/ADOPT or one-time MIGRATE, never by silent READY reset
